items.question:
A compliance analyst at a 400-person insurance firm starts a new Claude chat every time she reviews vendor contracts — three or four times a week — pasting the same policy thresholds and evaluation criteria at the start of each session. A colleague suggests she create a Claude Project.

What is the PRIMARY signal that a Project is justified here?

options.A: The same instructions and reference context recur across many sessions, making per-session setup wasteful.
options.B: Vendor contracts contain confidential data that should be isolated from other chat histories.
options.C: Projects provide a larger context window, making it easier to analyse long contracts.
options.D: A shared Project lets the legal team passively audit her review conversations.

items.question:
A bid manager at a large engineering consultancy creates a Project for proposal writing and enters: "Be helpful with proposals." Three weeks later, the team reports inconsistency — some outputs are punchy executive summaries, others dense technical narratives, and formatting varies from bid to bid.

What is the MOST likely cause of this inconsistency?

options.A: The Project knowledge base lacks sample proposals for Claude to calibrate its style against.
options.B: The project instruction is too vague to constrain output style, format, or audience orientation.
options.C: Different team members are using different model tiers within the same Project.
options.D: The instruction conflicts with Claude's default tone, causing unpredictable style overrides.

items.question:
A grant writer at a national non-profit creates a Project with the instruction: "Always use an optimistic, mission-driven tone and keep responses under 500 words." While drafting a government compliance report in that same Project, she types in the chat: "This section requires formal regulatory language and should run approximately 2,000 words."

How will Claude MOST likely handle this situation?

options.A: Claude will produce a 500-word response in optimistic tone because project instructions always take precedence.
options.B: Claude will flag the conflict and ask the user to reconcile the instructions before proceeding.
options.C: Claude will apply the chat instruction for this response, using formal regulatory language at approximately 2,000 words.
options.D: Claude will produce the full 2,000 words but still apply the optimistic tone as a compromise.

items.question:
A RevOps analyst at a 50-person SaaS startup has created nine Claude Projects over six months. His team repeatedly opens the wrong Project because names like "Marketing" and "Marketing 2" are ambiguous. He asks for advice on naming conventions.

What is the BEST practice for naming Projects to avoid this confusion?

options.A: Prefix all Project names with a sequential number and maintain a separate spreadsheet mapping numbers to purposes.
options.B: Limit the total number of Projects to five and archive the rest to enforce clarity through scarcity.
options.C: Use colour-coded emoji at the start of each name (e.g., "🔴 Marketing — Campaigns") to enable visual scanning.
options.D: Use names that include function, scope, and a limiting qualifier so the name alone identifies the Project's purpose.

items.question:
A procurement manager at a 12-person professional services firm has a Claude Project for reviewing supplier RFPs. She is the only user, but three new buyers are joining. She wants them to reach the same quality of RFP analysis she produces without lengthy coaching.

What is the MOST effective way to leverage the Project to achieve this?

options.A: Share the Project with the three buyers; ensure the custom instructions encode her evaluation criteria, scoring thresholds, and required output format.
options.B: Export the Project knowledge base as a PDF guide for buyers to read before they start their own independent chat sessions.
options.C: Ask each buyer to shadow her sessions for two weeks before gaining Project access, so they learn her prompting style.
options.D: Create separate Projects for each buyer with personalised instructions tailored to their individual experience levels.

items.question:
A clinical trials coordinator at a pharmaceutical company uses Claude for drafting regulatory correspondence. She starts a fresh chat each time and always pastes the trial sponsor name, protocol number, and the regulatory body's citation format before every query — a ritual she performs 10–15 times a week.

Which feature would MOST directly eliminate this repeated setup?

options.A: Uploading the citation style guide to each new chat as a reference document.
options.B: Creating a Project and placing the sponsor name, protocol number, and citation format in the custom instructions.
options.C: Saving the details as a local text file and using keyboard shortcuts to paste them faster.
options.D: Switching to a higher-tier model, which retains context from previous sessions.

items.question:
An internal communications manager at a 90,000-person bank must ensure all Claude-drafted all-staff emails follow the house style: sentences under 20 words, no passive voice, one-paragraph opening summary, sign-off "With appreciation." She creates a Project for this work.

Where should she encode these style constraints for MAXIMUM consistency across all drafts?

options.A: In the first message of each new chat session, so the constraints are visible and fresh for each draft.
options.B: In the Project knowledge base as a style-guide document that Claude can reference when prompted.
options.C: In the Project custom instructions, so they activate automatically for every session in the Project.
options.D: In a shared document outside Claude that all communicators consult before starting a session.

items.question:
A legal operations analyst at a global law firm configures a Project with: "Respond only in formal British English. Do not include legal advice. Always end responses with: 'This analysis is provided for informational purposes only.'" A visiting US client liaison uses the same Project and adds in her chat: "Please respond informally and use American spelling. Skip the disclaimer at the end."

Which TWO outcomes would MOST likely occur when the liaison sends her request? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Claude will adopt an informal register and American spelling, deferring to the more immediate per-chat instruction.
options.B: Claude will maintain formal British English, as project instructions take absolute precedence over per-chat requests.
options.C: The disclaimer will be omitted from this response, as the per-chat instruction explicitly removes it.
options.D: Claude will refuse to proceed because the per-chat instruction directly contradicts the project instruction.
options.E: The project owner will receive an automated notification that conflicting instructions were submitted.

items.question:
A VP of Customer Success at a 400-person SaaS company finds that the 12-person CSM team produces wildly inconsistent account health summaries — ranging from single-paragraph blurbs to seven-page narratives — and uses different renewal risk criteria per person. She wants to standardise output quality quickly.

What is the MOST efficient intervention?

options.A: Create a shared Project with custom instructions defining the required format, sections, and scoring criteria for health and risk assessments.
options.B: Circulate a prompting guide that each CSM reads and follows when using their own chat sessions.
options.C: Move the team to a higher-tier model, which produces more consistent and professional outputs.
options.D: Schedule monthly prompt calibration workshops where CSMs align on what a good summary looks like.

items.question:
A financial analyst at a hedge fund builds a Project for equity research and writes 47 instructions covering every task variant, exception, and edge case. Six months later, junior analysts who inherited the Project report erratic outputs — Claude sometimes follows conflicting rules and sometimes ignores instructions entirely, producing generic boilerplate.

What is the MOST likely root cause?

options.A: The Project has exceeded an instruction character limit, causing later instructions to be silently truncated.
options.B: The instruction set is internally contradictory and so long that Claude cannot reliably resolve conflicts or identify which rule applies to a given task.
options.C: The junior analysts are not prompting correctly, so their queries fail to activate the relevant instructions.
options.D: Model performance degrades over time as instruction-following capability diminishes with extended Project age.

items.question:
A retail chain inventory analyst needs Claude to help her interpret a one-time sales anomaly in a single region last quarter. She has the relevant data in a spreadsheet she will upload, and the task will not recur.

Which approach is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Use a standard single chat session, uploading the spreadsheet and asking the question directly.
options.B: Create a new Project so the analysis can be revisited if a similar anomaly occurs next quarter.
options.C: Add the spreadsheet to an existing inventory Project as a permanent knowledge document.
options.D: Use a Project with the spreadsheet in custom instructions so it loads automatically for all future inventory tasks.

items.question:
A care coordinator at a community health network creates a Project for patient outreach scripts. Her instruction reads: "Write empathetically and make sure the scripts are appropriate." Her team tries the Project and finds that script lengths range from 3 sentences to 15 paragraphs, and tone varies from clinical to conversational.

Which addition to the instruction would MOST directly fix the length and tone inconsistency?

options.A: Add patient demographic details to the knowledge base so Claude can calibrate tone to audience automatically.
options.B: Specify target length (e.g., 150–200 words), required sections (greeting, reason for contact, next step), and tone register (conversational, non-clinical).
options.C: Replace the instruction with a longer description of what empathy means in healthcare communication.
options.D: Provide three sample scripts in the knowledge base and instruct Claude to match their style.

items.question:
A quality assurance lead at a precision manufacturer creates a Project with the instruction: "Always recommend root cause analysis before proposing corrective actions." During an urgent production-line stoppage, an operator uses the same Project and types: "We have identified the root cause. Give me corrective action options immediately."

What is the MOST accurate description of how Claude will handle the operator's request?

options.A: Claude will provide corrective action options directly, since the per-chat instruction establishes that root cause analysis is complete and corrective actions are the needed output.
options.B: Claude will still prompt the user through a root cause analysis phase before providing corrective actions, as project instructions govern process steps.
options.C: Claude will ask the operator to confirm whether root cause analysis was performed before proceeding to corrective actions.
options.D: Claude will provide corrective actions but prepend a warning that root cause analysis should have been completed first.

items.question:
An administrator in a university research office manages Claude Projects for five different research groups — each group handles grants, publications, and compliance separately. She currently has 15 Projects with names like "Group A," "Group B Grants," and "Group C Compliance 2." Navigation is slow and mislabelling errors are increasing.

Which organisational approach would BEST improve navigation and reduce errors?

options.A: Reduce to one Project per research group and handle all tasks (grants, publications, compliance) within that single Project using per-chat instructions.
options.B: Adopt a consistent naming convention (e.g., "[Group Name] — [Function] — [Version/Year]") and archive Projects that are no longer active.
options.C: Delete all existing Projects and rebuild from scratch with a single shared Project for all five research groups.
options.D: Create a master index document that maps each Project name to its purpose and upload it to every Project's knowledge base.

items.question:
A policy analyst at a government agency uses a Claude Project for drafting consultation documents. She notices that details she shares in one conversation — the name of a specific stakeholder group and their position — are not available when she starts a new conversation in the same Project the next day.

What is the MOST accurate explanation for this behaviour?

options.A: The Project's storage quota was exceeded, causing recent conversation content to be deleted.
options.B: Claude requires users to manually save important conversation details to the Project knowledge base to persist them.
options.C: Project instructions persist across sessions, but conversation content within each chat does not carry over to new conversations.
options.D: The analyst's account permissions prevent the Project from retaining conversation history across days.

items.question:
A fleet operations manager at a logistics company is creating a Claude Project to help dispatchers draft driver briefing notes. He wants the outputs to be immediately usable without editing. He asks a consultant which elements should be included in the project custom instructions.

Which TWO elements would MOST directly improve output consistency and usability? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The required output format and structure (e.g., sections: Safety Reminders, Route Overview, Special Instructions; plain language; under 250 words).
options.B: A description of the company's history and the fleet operations department's reporting structure.
options.C: The names and shift schedules of individual dispatchers who will use the Project.
options.D: The audience characteristics and language register (e.g., audience is drivers with varying literacy levels; use plain language; avoid technical jargon).
options.E: A list of all the routes the company currently operates, stored as a static table.

items.question:
An HSE advisor at an energy company has been adding to her safety documentation Project's instructions for 18 months. The instruction set now contains 38 rules, including several that contradict each other because earlier rules were never removed when superseded. She notices Claude's outputs have become unpredictable — sometimes excellent, sometimes boilerplate.

Which maintenance action would MOST directly address the root cause?

options.A: Export the current instructions to a document, have the team review which rules are still valid, remove contradictions, and rewrite to a concise non-contradictory set.
options.B: Add a new instruction at the top of the set that reads: "Prioritise the most recently added rule when conflicts arise."
options.C: Reset the Project by deleting all instructions and starting from a blank slate, then add rules only as they are needed.
options.D: Split the Project into multiple specialised Projects, each with its own focused instruction set.

items.question:
A brand communications specialist at a telecoms company is configuring a Claude Project for drafting customer-facing social media responses. The brand guidelines specify: assertive but empathetic, first-person plural ('we'), no exclamation points, and acknowledgement of the customer's frustration before pivoting to resolution. She wants Claude to apply these consistently without reminding it each session.

What is the MOST appropriate location for these brand voice requirements?

options.A: In the Project custom instructions, so the brand voice parameters activate automatically in every conversation.
options.B: In the first message of each conversation, prefaced with 'Remember our brand guidelines.'.
options.C: In the Project knowledge base alongside the full brand guidelines document for Claude to reference.
options.D: In a separate Claude conversation specifically for defining the brand persona, then copied into each drafting session.

items.question:
A social media coordinator at a media company asks whether she should create a Claude Project for each of the following two tasks: (1) drafting a one-time tribute post for a retiring colleague, and (2) writing weekly audience engagement summaries in the company's established report format for the next 12 months.

Which TWO statements best describe the appropriate approach for these tasks? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Task 1 warrants a Project because the tribute post requires careful, personalised tone that Claude must learn over time.
options.B: Task 1 does not warrant a Project because it is a one-off task with no recurring setup cost.
options.C: Task 2 warrants a Project because the same report format and audience context apply week after week.
options.D: Task 2 does not warrant a Project because the format can be included in a per-chat prompt each week.
options.E: Both tasks warrant Projects because any task involving specific format requirements should be managed in a Project.

items.question:
A regulatory affairs analyst at a pharmaceutical company creates a Project for summarising clinical study results for different audiences. Her project instruction reads: "Summarise clinical studies clearly." She finds that outputs intended for principal investigators read the same as those intended for patient advocacy groups — full of statistical terms neither group finds accessible.

Which instruction change would MOST directly fix this?

options.A: Add an instruction to 'avoid jargon' to reduce statistical terminology across all summaries.
options.B: Upload example summaries for each audience type to the knowledge base and instruct Claude to match the appropriate one.
options.C: Add an audience-calibration instruction specifying how terminology and complexity should vary by stated audience (e.g., 'When audience is specified as patients or advocates, use plain language and no statistical notation; when audience is investigators, use standard clinical terminology').
options.D: Create a separate Project for each audience type with tailored instructions for that audience's needs.

items.question:
An underwriting analyst at a specialty insurer creates a Project with the instruction: "Do not provide risk ratings or coverage recommendations — provide analysis only." During a session, a colleague types: "I need you to rate this risk as acceptable, borderline, or unacceptable and recommend whether to bind coverage."

How will Claude MOST likely respond?

options.A: Claude will provide a risk rating and recommendation, deferring to the per-chat instruction as the more immediate directive.
options.B: Claude will provide the analysis it can offer but is likely to decline the rating and recommendation, as those dimensions are explicitly prohibited in the project instruction and no per-chat context resolves the restriction.
options.C: Claude will ask the project owner to clarify whether the per-chat instruction is permitted before proceeding.
options.D: Claude will provide the rating but omit the recommendation, applying a partial override to the project instruction.

items.question:
A knowledge management associate at a mid-size law firm is preparing to share a Claude Project — used for drafting client advice summaries — with six junior associates. The Project knowledge base contains the firm's standard clause library and three precedent documents. She asks which access considerations she should address before sharing.

Which TWO considerations are MOST important to address before sharing? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Whether the junior associates have received training on Claude's limitations and the need to verify factual claims in legal documents.
options.B: Whether the custom instructions clearly specify the output format and review requirements so associates know what to check before sending advice to clients.
options.C: Whether the precedent documents in the knowledge base are current and authorised versions, not superseded or draft materials.
options.D: Whether the firm's internal billing system can track which associate used the Project for which client matter.
options.E: Whether each associate prefers a different writing style that the Project instructions should accommodate.

items.question:
A fundraising manager at a small non-profit is setting up her first Claude Project for donor communications. She has never written project instructions before and asks what she should write first.

What is the MOST useful first instruction to write for this Project?

options.A: The required output format and any content that must appear in every donor communication (e.g., the mission statement reference, call to action, sign-off name).
options.B: A detailed history of the organisation and the names of all current major donors.
options.C: An instruction to always check for grammatical errors before presenting the output.
options.D: A list of topics the organisation would never discuss publicly, to prevent Claude from mentioning them.

items.question:
A product manager at a retail bank is deciding how to organise Claude Projects for her team. She manages two major workstreams: (1) customer communications — FAQs, email templates, and chatbot scripts — and (2) internal product documentation — feature specs, release notes, and roadmap summaries. Both workstreams are active simultaneously.

Which Project structure is MOST appropriate?

options.A: One unified Project covering both workstreams, with instructions addressing both customer-facing and internal documentation requirements.
options.B: One Project per team member who works on each workstream, to allow personalisation of tone and format preferences.
options.C: Two separate Projects — one for customer communications and one for internal documentation — each with its own focused instructions and knowledge base.
options.D: A single Project for all tasks, with instructions telling Claude to detect the workstream from context and apply the appropriate standards automatically.

items.question:
An operations coordinator at an automotive parts manufacturer has been asked to set up a Claude Project for her production planning team. She has drafted the project instructions and uploaded three reference documents to the knowledge base. She has not yet tested the Project. Several colleagues are waiting to start using it Monday morning.

What should she do NEXT?

options.A: Share the Project with the team immediately so they can test it themselves during their actual Monday tasks.
options.B: Add more reference documents to the knowledge base before testing, to ensure Claude has comprehensive context.
options.C: Ask IT to approve the Project configuration before any testing or sharing occurs.
options.D: Test the Project with 3–5 representative tasks to verify the instructions produce the expected output before sharing with the team.

items.question:
A learning and development manager at a 3,000-person pharmaceutical company is setting up a Claude Project to help curriculum authors produce consistent training materials. She must decide which documents to add to Project knowledge.

Which content type BEST fits Project knowledge for this use case?

options.A: The company writing style guide and an approved medical terminology glossary.
options.B: The roster of employees enrolled in this quarter's compliance training cohort.
options.C: A transcript from last month's curriculum planning meeting.
options.D: A draft module script that is still awaiting SME sign-off.

items.question:
A procurement specialist at a 90,000-person logistics firm uses a Claude Project for supplier negotiations. Project knowledge includes a supplier price list uploaded 14 months ago. A new price list was issued six weeks ago but has not been added. Claude is quoting figures from the old list.

What is the MOST direct cause?

options.A: Claude's training data does not include the supplier's recent pricing updates.
options.B: The outdated price list is still in Project knowledge and has not been replaced by the current version.
options.C: The Project's connector lost synchronisation with the procurement system.
options.D: The supplier updated prices after Claude generated the response.

items.question:
A compliance analyst at a global bank has discovered that a Claude Project used for AML reviews contains both the superseded 2022 AML policy and the current 2024 policy. Claude's draft compliance memos have been citing approval thresholds from the 2022 version.

What should the analyst do FIRST?

options.A: Add a note to the Project custom instructions warning Claude that the 2022 policy has been superseded.
options.B: Ask Claude to prefix each memo with a disclaimer that some referenced thresholds may be outdated.
options.C: Remove the 2022 policy from Project knowledge and confirm the 2024 policy is the sole version present.
options.D: Wait for the compliance documentation team to formally archive the 2022 policy before making any changes.

items.question:
A technical writer at a 40-person software startup has uploaded six product specification documents to a Claude Project. Every file is named generically: spec_v1.docx through spec_v6.docx. When asking Claude questions about specific features, she gets inconsistent answers that mix details from the wrong products.

Which naming approach would MOST directly reduce this problem?

options.A: Add a numeric priority prefix to each file (e.g., 01-spec.docx) so Claude processes them in order.
options.B: Prefix each file with its upload date (e.g., 2024-03-01-spec.docx) to establish a clear timeline.
options.C: Use brief acronyms derived from product names (e.g., PGAPI.docx) to keep filenames short.
options.D: Use descriptive names that identify the product, module, and document type (e.g., PaymentGateway-API-Spec.docx).

items.question:
An HR business partner at a 12-person fintech startup needs Claude to compare a single candidate's resume against a job description for a one-off senior hire. Neither document will be needed after this conversation.

Which approach is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Upload both documents directly in the conversation rather than adding them to a Claude Project.
options.B: Create a new Claude Project for this candidate and add both documents to its knowledge base.
options.C: Add the job description to the existing HR Project as permanent knowledge for future hiring cycles.
options.D: Ask Claude to search the web for the candidate's public professional profile instead of uploading the resume.

items.question:
A bid manager at a 400-person professional services firm uses a Claude Project to draft client proposals. Project knowledge contains two proposal templates: the original 2022 brand template and an updated 2024 version that superseded it. Claude is producing proposals that blend formatting rules from both templates.

What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Upload a third 'master' template that explicitly merges the best elements of both versions.
options.B: Remove the 2022 template from Project knowledge and confirm only the 2024 version remains.
options.C: Rename both templates to include their year in the filename and add an instruction to prefer the newer one.
options.D: Add a Project instruction telling Claude to always use the 2024 template rules.

items.question:
A clinical coordinator at an 11,000-staff hospital network is setting up a Claude Project to help nursing staff look up care protocols. She proposes adding last week's de-identified patient encounter notes to Project knowledge, reasoning that real case examples will make protocol guidance more relevant.

What is the MOST significant concern with this approach?

options.A: De-identified encounter notes are too short to provide meaningful context for protocol questions.
options.B: Adding only last week's notes creates recency bias; a broader date range should be used first.
options.C: Patient encounter notes — even de-identified — are operational records rather than stable reference content, and create ongoing data lifecycle obligations in the knowledge base.
options.D: The notes should be encrypted before upload to comply with data governance requirements.

items.question:
A grant writer at a 15-person environmental non-profit has added 47 documents to a Claude Project over six months: grant applications, funder reports, meeting notes, and donor communications. Claude's responses have become generic and frequently miss specific program details that are clearly present in the uploaded files.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The Project needs a higher-tier model with more advanced reasoning to handle the volume.
options.B: The grant writer should add more context in each chat prompt to compensate for the large knowledge base.
options.C: Claude should be asked to summarise the entire knowledge base at the start of each session.
options.D: The knowledge base has grown too large and unfocused, diluting the relevance of the specific program content.

items.question:
A content strategist at a 200-person media company set up a Claude Project for editorial style and tone guidance. Over four months, Project knowledge has grown to 22 documents, now including competitor intelligence reports, social media trend analyses, and market research briefs added opportunistically.

Which statement BEST describes the situation?

options.A: The Project is well-stocked; a richer knowledge base always improves the relevance of Claude's outputs.
options.B: The Project should have its knowledge base capped at 20 documents to prevent further accumulation.
options.C: The competitor intelligence and market content represent off-topic additions that dilute the Project's editorial focus.
options.D: An index document listing every file should be added so Claude can navigate the knowledge base more effectively.

items.question:
A RevOps analyst at a 600-person SaaS company maintains a Claude Project used by account executives to research deal context. Project knowledge contains a CRM opportunity export (CSV) uploaded three months ago. AEs report that Claude regularly cites stale deal stages and outdated ARR figures.

What change would MOST effectively keep this knowledge current?

options.A: Schedule a weekly manual re-export and re-upload of the CRM data.
options.B: Replace the static CSV upload with a CRM connector that keeps Project knowledge synchronised with live CRM data.
options.C: Add a Project instruction noting that CRM data may be up to 90 days old and AEs should verify independently.
options.D: Archive the Project and ask AEs to query the CRM directly instead of using Claude.

items.question:
An internal auditor at a 250-store retail chain uploaded a 180-page internal audit manual as a single unstructured PDF to a Claude Project. Claude frequently cites generic audit principles rather than the specific controls and thresholds defined for different store types.

What structural change would MOST improve response specificity?

options.A: Split the PDF into equal 30-page chunks and upload each chunk as a separate file.
options.B: Add a one-page summary at the beginning of the PDF listing chapter topics.
options.C: Restructure the document with clear, descriptive section headings that identify store type and control category, or split along those semantic dimensions.
options.D: Convert the PDF to a Word document so Claude can process it more accurately.

items.question:
An actuarial analyst at a 2,000-person insurance company has uploaded three versions of the mortality assumption table to a shared actuarial Claude Project: MortTable_v1.xlsx, MortTable_v2.xlsx, and MortTable_v3.xlsx. Only v3 is current. Colleagues report that Claude draws figures from all three versions across different sessions.

What is the CORRECT action?

options.A: Add a Project instruction that tells Claude to always use the file with the highest version number.
options.B: Rename v3 to 'MortTable_Current.xlsx' while keeping v1 and v2 for audit trail purposes.
options.C: Combine all three tables into one workbook with clearly labelled tabs showing the version history.
options.D: Remove v1 and v2 from Project knowledge, leaving only v3 as the sole active document.

items.question:
A legal counsel at an 80,000-person energy company shares a contract review Claude Project with three junior solicitors. Project knowledge contains approved clause libraries and internal contracting policy. During an active acquisition, counsel begins uploading deal-specific side letters and preliminary negotiation positions to the same Project.

What is the PRIMARY risk introduced by this approach?

options.A: Deal-specific negotiation positions are ephemeral and sensitive documents that will mislead future reviews once the deal closes or positions change, and may exceed the access scope of junior solicitors.
options.B: The clause library and policy documents will conflict with the deal-specific content, degrading the quality of all contract reviews.
options.C: Junior solicitors may lack the seniority to view acquisition documents, constituting a training-level access violation.
options.D: Uploading large side letters may degrade Project performance by increasing the total knowledge base size.

items.question:
An IT governance manager at a 5,000-person public sector agency oversees a Claude Project shared with eight procurement analysts. A team lead proposes adding completed vendor risk assessment questionnaires — which contain detailed vendor security architecture and network topology information — to the Project knowledge base.

What is the MOST important action before proceeding?

options.A: Redact the network topology sections from each questionnaire before uploading.
options.B: Verify the data handling classification of vendor security content and confirm that storing it in an AI Project is consistent with third-party confidentiality obligations.
options.C: Confirm that all eight analysts hold the appropriate clearance level for each specific vendor's security information.
options.D: Convert the questionnaire responses to a standardised format to ensure Claude can parse them accurately.

items.question:
A sourcing manager at a 12,000-person automotive manufacturer uploaded a 220-page supplier qualification framework as a single document. When asked about requirements for specific supplier categories (castings, electronics, logistics), Claude gives accurate but generic answers that apply to all suppliers rather than citing category-specific criteria.

What is the MOST effective structural remedy?

options.A: Rewrite the chat prompt to specify the page range relevant to each supplier category.
options.B: Add a one-page executive summary at the front of the document listing the categories covered.
options.C: Split the framework into separate documents, one per supplier category, with descriptive filenames and clear internal headings.
options.D: Ask Claude to read the whole framework and produce its own summary of category-specific requirements.

items.question:
A marketing operations manager at a 40-person hospitality group is building a Claude Project to help the team produce consistent guest communications and campaign content. She must decide which documents to add to Project knowledge.

Which TWO items are MOST appropriate for permanent Project knowledge? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The group's brand tone and voice guidelines (approved, version-controlled, applies to all communications).
options.B: A list of VIP guests who attended last month's event and their dietary preferences.
options.C: An internal email thread in which the team debated the summer campaign tagline.
options.D: The approved food and beverage menu template used across all three properties.
options.E: A draft version of the upcoming loyalty programme announcement, pending legal review.

items.question:
A data analyst at a 25,000-person telecoms company is reviewing a shared Claude Project used by the analytics team. She wants to identify whether Project knowledge needs curation.

Which TWO conditions are the STRONGEST indicators that curation is required? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The Project knowledge currently contains eight documents.
options.B: Three documents have nearly identical names but contain different content.
options.C: Claude cited a network benchmarking report from four years ago as current industry performance data.
options.D: The Project was created six months ago and has not been modified since.
options.E: One of the documents is a 60-page PDF rather than a shorter summary.

items.question: A finance controller at an eight-hospital healthcare system manages a Claude Project used by the finance team to draft regulatory capital reports. She is establishing a document lifecycle policy for Project knowledge. Which THREE practices would MOST directly improve and maintain knowledge base freshness? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Assign a named owner and a next-review date to each document, recorded in a separate register.
options.B: Cap the total Project knowledge at a maximum of 15 documents regardless of content needs.
options.C: When uploading a new version of a document, remove the prior version in the same session.
options.D: Store all Project documents in a shared folder outside the AI tool for backup purposes.
options.E: Trigger a knowledge base review each time a referenced regulatory standard or internal policy is officially updated.

items.question: A solutions architect at a global investment bank is evaluating which Project knowledge inputs justify using a connector rather than periodic static uploads. Which TWO scenarios are MOST appropriate for a connector? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The bank's annual corporate branding guide, refreshed once per year.
options.B: The live deal pipeline from the investment banking tracking system, queried daily by deal teams.
options.C: A PDF of the Basel capital adequacy framework, which changes only when regulators issue new guidance.
options.D: Daily summarised customer service tickets refreshed each morning for a client-facing support triage team.
options.E: The employee benefits handbook, updated annually at open enrolment.

items.question:
